notes: Tina Lindstrom is a Partner at First NY, where she manages an oil volatility portfolio. She began her career at Susquehanna and eventually worked her way up to managing both the high cap equity index group and the commodity volatility group. This gives her the unique perspective to be able to compare and contrast how these two markets operate. Tina explains what makes commodity markets unique, how the structure of markets has changed over time, how relative value trades might emerge, and what happens when you’re trading volatility and front-month futures go negative. Please enjoy my conversation with Tina Lindstrom.

thesis: The episode introduces Tina Lindstrom, a partner at First New York who manages an oil volatility portfolio and previously worked at Susquehanna managing equity index and commodity volatility groups. She explains that while equity index volatility typically exhibits a skew where fear is concentrated in downside moves, commodity volatility usually exhibits the opposite skew where fear is concentrated in upside moves due to supply shortages, though crude oil volatility can resemble equity-style volatility until a specific event causes it to flip back to the typical commodity pattern.
